picks.title: Maxon's Fall 2026 Release Brings Bigger Worlds, Faster Workflows, and Major Updates
picks.excerpt: Maxon's fall release adds Red Giant Scene Light, an AI-powered depth-aware relighting tool for live-action footage and CG renders after the shoot, plus an MCP server that lets AI agents drive Autograph.
picks.rationale: A shipping tool release: Red Giant Scene Light relights footage after the shoot using AI depth, and Autograph gets an MCP server for AI agents. This changes how motion and post artists work tomorrow.

picks.title: Astra Studios Launches AstraLabs, Teams with VerSe on AI Pipeline
picks.excerpt: The Hombale Group-backed Astra Studios and Dailyhunt parent VerSe will co-develop and market an AI-native pipeline built on SparkStation that carries a production from script to distribution while keeping faces, wardrobe and locations consistent across shots; announced at MIPCOM.
picks.rationale: A new MIPCOM announcement: a studio backed by a major Indian producer launches an AI-native pipeline that runs from script to distribution, with a focus on keeping characters and locations consistent across shots.

picks.title: Nobody is safe from celebrity AI deepfakes
picks.excerpt: Social feeds are filling with AI-generated images of actors and stars, and Meta doesn't require labels for AI-generated still images, leaving performers' likenesses largely unprotected.
picks.rationale: An industry-wide report, not the single Mia Goth incident: it finds that Meta does not label AI-generated still images, which leaves performers' likenesses unprotected across platforms. That matters for anyone making or promoting talent imagery.

picks.title: Critics Vindicate 'Artificial' After Messy Amazon MGM Breakup (and the Studios vs. Talent Wars Around AI Are Just Beginning)
picks.excerpt: Luca Guadagnino's OpenAI drama 'Artificial' earned acclaim after Amazon MGM dropped it; Variety frames it as the opening of a wider studios-vs-talent fight over AI.
picks.rationale: A studio dropped a prestige film about OpenAI, and critics then praised it. Variety reads this as the start of a wider fight between studios and talent over AI, a story not covered before in this section.

picks.title: Animation And VFX Leaders Discuss AI And Jobs At View Conference
picks.excerpt: At View Conference, executives from Sony Pictures Imageworks, ILM, Skydance, Cinesite and others discussed shifting pipelines and AI; ILM's Janet Lewin warned against treating AI as a 'magic bullet' while Opsis's Laurens Ehrmann said AI 'can compress execution time, but it cannot compress taste.'
picks.rationale: A different View session from the published Netflix/Eyeline talk: heads of Imageworks, ILM, Skydance and Cinesite discuss how AI is changing pipelines and jobs.

alternates.title: This Hack Fixes Your AI Character Consistency Issues (Pro Workflow)
alternates.excerpt: Curious Refuge compares two popular AI character-consistency methods for AI filmmaking, with a written breakdown and prompts for building pro character sheets.
alternates.rationale: Actionable tutorial; held back because a character-consistency workflow video ran on 09-26.

alternates.title: Accounting for the New Economics of VFX
alternates.excerpt: VFX vendors are rethinking bids as AI raises per-artist output on roto and cleanup, alongside tax incentives and remote pipelines reshaping the economics of visual effects.
